**Notes for Monday, Oct 12, 2026 (TSX)**

- **No trading today.** Monday, Oct 12 is the Canadian Thanksgiving long weekend. One report says Canada's stock market returned from the Thanksgiving long weekend on Tuesday, October 13. I found no TSX trading data for Oct 12 itself.
- **Last close before today (Friday, Oct 9):** The S&P/TSX Composite closed at 35,664.62, up 519.24 points (+1.48%), per MSN Money. Trading Economics ties the gain to weaker employment data reinforcing expectations that the Bank of Canada will refrain from hiking rates.
- **Results dated after "today."** Several results describe Tuesday, Oct 13 and Wednesday, Oct 14, which is later than the date I was given. Treat them as possibly mismatched with the stated date.
  - The TMX quote page shows an Oct 13 close of 35,983.98, up 319.36 (0.895%). Investing.com, Trading Economics and The Canadian Vanguard report the same close, about +0.9%.
  - One outlet (Sunday Guardian) reports a different Oct 13 close of 35,867.03, up 0.57%. This disagrees with TMX and the other sources. TMX is the exchange's own page.
  - The Oct 13 move was bolstered by a jump in energy-sector shares and steadying bond yields.
  - The Canadian Vanguard says the index has now advanced for three consecutive sessions, recovering from last Wednesday's brutal sell-off.
- **Range:** The 52-week range on the TMX page is 29,530.92 to 37,069.11. Trading Economics puts the index up 18.52% from a year earlier.
